annotation_description: Playing Shadowy Backstreet on turn 1 means the land enters tapped, preventing the player from casting Aether Vial on turn 1. Aether Vial is one of the most important turn 1 plays in Death & Taxes / Eldrazi strategies, as each turn it's delayed costs a charge counter and tempo. Playing Karakas or Scrubland would allow casting Aether Vial immediately on turn 1, which is critical for the deck's game plan.

Missed the opportunity to deploy Glaring Fleshraker on Turn 1 by playing Ancient Tomb + Lotus Petal for 3 colorless mana ({2}{C}). Instead played Cavern of Souls which produces only 1 mana and doesn't enable any Turn 1 play, losing a full turn of tempo with a key synergy piece.

Casting Aether Vial before playing a land is a sequencing error. The player should play a land first (Karakas, Scrubland, or Wasteland) to have more mana available and more information before committing to casting spells. Playing a land first is free and doesn't cost anything. Specifically, playing Karakas or Wasteland first would leave Shadowy Backstreet untapped to still cast Aether Vial, while also developing the mana base. With two Aether Vials in hand, the player could potentially play a land, cast one Vial off Shadowy Backstreet, and still have options. More importantly, playing land before spells is a fundamental sequencing principle - you never want to cast spells before making your land drop unless there's a specific reason.

Playing Karakas instead of Wasteland or Scrubland is suboptimal. The opponent has Cavern of Souls (likely naming Eldrazi), which is a high-priority target for Wasteland. Playing Wasteland now would allow destroying Cavern of Souls on the opponent's next turn before they can develop further. Alternatively, playing Scrubland would allow casting Stoneforge Mystic this turn (tapping Scrubland for W and using Aether Vial's 0 counters won't work yet - Vial has 1 counter after upkeep trigger). Actually, Aether Vial should have 1 counter now (beginning of turn 2 upkeep), so it could vial in a 1-CMC creature but neither Phelia nor Stoneforge is CMC 1. So the Vial can't put in creatures yet. Playing Scrubland would let them cast Aether Vial (already on board) or hold up mana. Actually, with Karakas providing W, they can't cast Stoneforge (needs 1W = 2 mana) with just one land. With Scrubland, same issue - only one land producing W. So for casting purposes, Karakas and Scrubland are equivalent this turn. However, Wasteland would be better as the land drop to threaten the opponent's Cavern of Souls, which is their only land. Destroying Cavern would be devastating for the opponent's development. Karakas's bounce ability is less immediately relevant.

KimiK2 declined to activate Aether Vial (which has 0 charge counters, so it can't put anything useful into play) BUT more importantly, they had mana available to cast Aether Vial from hand (the second copy) using Karakas for {W} — wait, Aether Vial costs {1} so Karakas could pay for it. However, looking more carefully: they already have an Aether Vial on the battlefield and a second one in hand. They could cast the second Aether Vial using Karakas (tap for {W} which can pay the {1} generic cost). Having two Aether Vials would let them deploy creatures at two different CMCs simultaneously in future turns. But actually, the bigger issue is that they should have played their land drop (Scrubland or Wasteland) this turn — the board shows only Shadowy Backstreet and Karakas as lands, and they have Scrubland and Wasteland in hand. They missed playing a land this turn, which delays their mana development. Wait — the reasoning says 'With my land play already used this turn' but looking at the board, there are only 2 lands (Shadowy Backstreet from turn 1, Karakas presumably played turn 2). So the land drop was used. The real question is whether to cast the second Aether Vial. With Karakas untapped, they could tap it for {W} to cast the second Aether Vial, giving them two Vials ticking up at different rates. This is a reasonable play in D&T strategies. Additionally, they could have played Wasteland or Scrubland as their land and used that mana. But if the land was already played (Karakas this turn), then they should still tap Karakas to cast the second Aether Vial to maximize tempo.

The player chose to play Ancient Tomb instead of casting Chalice of the Void. With Lotus Petal + Ancient Tomb already available (or Cavern of Souls + Lotus Petal), they could potentially cast Chalice of the Void for X=1, which would be extremely powerful against the opponent's Death & Taxes style deck running Aether Vial (already on board, so it dodges Chalice, but future 1-mana spells like Swords to Plowshares, Mother of Runes, etc. would be countered). However, the player played a land they can't use this turn (already had Cavern of Souls). The question is whether Chalice on 1 is worth it here - the opponent already has Aether Vial in play, so many of their creatures will bypass Chalice. But Chalice on 1 still shuts off a significant portion of D&T's spells. Playing Ancient Tomb first is fine if they plan to cast Chalice next, but they could have cast Chalice for X=1 using Cavern of Souls + Lotus Petal (sacrificing petal for colorless), saving the Ancient Tomb play for later when they need the mana for bigger spells. The sequencing matters because Ancient Tomb deals 2 damage each time it's tapped.

Chalice on 0 is a reasonable play against Death & Taxes variants that might run Lotus Petal or other 0-cost cards, but the opponent already has Aether Vial in play (which is the main 1-drop target for Chalice). Chalice on 1 would counter future Aether Vials, Swords to Plowshares, and other key 1-mana spells in Death & Taxes. With Ancient Tomb + Cavern of Souls, the player could cast Chalice on X=1 for 2 mana. Additionally, Chalice on 0 counters the player's own Lotus Petal if they ever want to cast another one. The opponent appears to be on Death & Taxes (Karakas, Aether Vial, Stoneforge Mystic deck), where Chalice on 1 hitting Swords to Plowshares, Mother of Runes, and similar 1-drops would be much more impactful than Chalice on 0. However, Glaring Fleshraker on turn 2 (using Ancient Tomb + Cavern of Souls naming Eldrazi) could also be a strong play to start generating value from colorless spells.

Pre-War Formalwear's key value is its ETB reanimation trigger, but KimiK2's graveyard is empty, so casting it wastes its primary effect. It just enters as an unattached equipment with no creature to equip (costs 3 more to equip). Meanwhile, Stoneforge Mystic would tutor an equipment AND provide a body, all for 2 mana, leaving mana open.

Chalice of the Void is on the battlefield with 0 charge counters (cast for X=0, entering with 0 counters). Aether Vial costs {1}, so Chalice doesn't counter it. However, the key issue is sequencing: casting Phelia before Stoneforge Mystic is suboptimal. Stoneforge Mystic should be cast first to tutor an Equipment card (like Kaldra Compleat or Batterskull), setting up the Stoneforge activation on the next turn. With Pre-War Formalwear already in hand, the Stoneforge tutor could find a different powerful equipment. Additionally, Phelia is a legendary creature vulnerable to the opponent's Karakas... wait, Karakas is on KimiK2's side. But the opponent has Cavern of Souls. More importantly, the Aether Vial currently has 1 counter (it's turn 3, Vial entered turn 1, got a counter turn 2 and turn 3 upkeeps = 2 counters). Actually, let me reconsider - the Vial has been getting counters. With 2 counters on Aether Vial, KimiK2 could Vial in a 2-drop creature for free. Both Phelia and Stoneforge Mystic are 2-drops. The correct play is to cast Stoneforge Mystic (to get the ETB tutor trigger) and then use Aether Vial to put Phelia onto the battlefield for free, getting both creatures this turn. Instead, by casting Phelia, they waste the Vial opportunity since they could have Vialed Phelia in. Now they'll need to either cast Stoneforge next turn or Vial it in, but casting it would have been better this turn to maximize tempo.

KimiK2 declined to activate Aether Vial (which has 1 charge counter from upkeep triggers) to put Stoneforge Mystic (mana value 2) onto the battlefield... wait, let me check. Aether Vial was played turn 1, so by turn 3 it should have 2 counters (one added turn 2 upkeep, one added turn 3 upkeep). With 2 counters, they could vial in Stoneforge Mystic (MV 2) for free, which would tutor an equipment card. Additionally, they have Scrubland untapped and could cast the second Aether Vial for 1 mana, but Chalice of the Void is on the battlefield. We need to check what X Chalice was cast for - it was cast with Ancient Tomb (2 colorless) + Lotus Petal (still on battlefield untapped) + Cavern of Souls. Actually, looking at the board, Chalice is on the battlefield and Lotus Petal is still there. Given Ancient Tomb + Cavern of Souls were tapped, and the opponent had Lotus Petal and Kozilek's Command in graveyard, Chalice was likely cast for X=1 (costing {1}{1} = 2 mana from Ancient Tomb). This means casting the second Aether Vial (MV 1) would be countered by Chalice. But activating the existing Aether Vial to put in Stoneforge Mystic is an activated ability, not a spell, so Chalice doesn't interact with it. Declining to vial in Stoneforge Mystic means missing a free creature deployment that tutors equipment (like Kaldra Compleat or Batterskull), which is a significant tempo and value loss.

Playing Reality Smasher is a strong tempo play, but Thought-Knot Seer might be better here. The opponent has Aether Vial (currently at 1 or 2 counters) and could be holding powerful cards like Stoneforge Mystic targets or removal. TKS would strip a key card from their hand while also providing a solid 4/4 body. Additionally, Phelia can flicker TKS for card disadvantage if it attacks, but the hand disruption on entry is still valuable. Reality Smasher's trample and haste are strong, but Phelia could blink it (forcing a card draw for the opponent when it leaves) and it doesn't address what the opponent might be holding. However, Reality Smasher does present a faster clock with haste, so this is debatable.

Blocking Reality Smasher (5/5 with trample) with Phelia (2/2) is a poor trade. Phelia dies, and trample still deals 3 damage through. Phelia is a high-value creature that generates card advantage through her exile/flicker ability and is key to the Death & Taxes strategy. By blocking, KimiK2 loses Phelia to save only 2 life (taking 3 trample damage instead of 5). Additionally, Phelia could have been protected by not blocking and instead used on future attacks to exile opponent's threats like Chalice of the Void or Reality Smasher itself. The player also has Pre-War Formalwear in hand which could bring Phelia back, but that's a 3-mana investment that could be used more efficiently. Taking 5 damage (going to 15) while keeping Phelia on board would have been significantly better than losing this key creature to save 2 life.

chosen_display: Wasteland — {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Destroy target nonbasic la... [Activate]
annotation_description: Casting Stoneforge Mystic for mana when Aether Vial has 2 charge counters and could put SFM onto the battlefield for free. By casting SFM, they spend 2 mana and can't also cast Pre-War Formalwear (costs 3) this turn. Using Vial for SFM would leave all lands untapped to cast Formalwear, which would reanimate Phelia from the graveyard - a much more powerful turn.

KimiK2 Vorthos declined to activate Aether Vial (which has charge counters on it) during their precombat main phase. With Stoneforge Mystic already on board, they could use Stoneforge's activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}) to put Batterskull directly onto the battlefield, which would create a 4/4 vigilance lifelink Germ token — excellent against Reality Smasher. However, even without that line, declining to use Aether Vial's free creature deployment ability is leaving value on the table. The Vial activation is a pure upside free ability that costs no mana. Additionally, they skipped their attack phase with Stoneforge Mystic available (though attacking into Reality Smasher would be poor). The key miss is not using Stoneforge Mystic's ability to put Batterskull onto the battlefield this turn — Scrubland provides {W}, and between Scrubland and other lands they should have access to {1}{W} to activate Stoneforge. With Batterskull on the field, the 4/4 lifelink token would help stabilize against Reality Smasher significantly.

Playing Ancient Tomb as the land drop instead of Eye of Ugin loses significant tempo. Eye of Ugin reduces colorless Eldrazi costs by 2, enabling casting both Glaring Fleshraker (effectively 1 mana) and Thought-Knot Seer (effectively 2 mana) in the same turn for only 3 of the 4 available mana. Ancient Tomb only provides 6 total mana, insufficient to cast both (7 mana needed). This misses deploying an extra creature and the Fleshraker triggers.

Playing Eye of Ugin as the land drop sacrifices City of Traitors (which produces {C}{C}), replacing it with Eye of Ugin (which only produces {C} via tap, or provides a cost reduction for colorless Eldrazi spells). The player loses 2 colorless mana production this turn. With City of Traitors + Ancient Tomb + Cavern of Souls + Lotus Petal, the player had 7 mana available (2+2+1+1 from lands, plus Lotus Petal for 1) and could cast Thought-Knot Seer (costs 3C = 4 mana) before playing the land. After sacrificing City of Traitors to Eye of Ugin, the available mana drops significantly. The player could have cast Thought-Knot Seer first using City of Traitors mana, THEN played Eye of Ugin. With Eye of Ugin's cost reduction, they might have even been able to cast a second creature. Instead, by playing Eye of Ugin first, they lose City of Traitors' mana before using it, significantly reducing what they can deploy this turn.

Blocking Reality Smasher (5/5 with trample) with Stoneforge Mystic (1/2) is a terrible trade. Stoneforge Mystic dies, 4 trample damage still gets through (so only 1 damage is prevented), and KimiK2 loses their most important creature — the one that can cheat Batterskull into play for just 1W. Stoneforge Mystic with Batterskull in hand is an incredibly valuable piece that should not be thrown away to prevent 1 point of damage. Without Stoneforge, they'll need to hardcast Batterskull for 5 mana, which is much slower and may not happen against the Eldrazi pressure.

With Eye of Ugin reducing costs by 2, Glaring Fleshraker costs just 1 mana and Thought-Knot Seer costs just 2 mana. Casting Fleshraker first, then TKS, would net an extra Eldrazi Spawn token and 1 damage to opponent from Fleshraker's triggers. Casting TKS first (or alone) misses these synergy triggers.

KimiK2 Vorthos declined to activate Wasteland during their upkeep, missing the opportunity to destroy a key nonbasic land like Eye of Ugin (which reduces Eldrazi costs by 2) or Ancient Tomb (which provides 2 colorless mana). Eye of Ugin is particularly important to destroy as it makes all of the opponent's Eldrazi spells significantly cheaper. The opponent has a Reality Smasher already in play and Eye of Ugin will continue to enable undercosted Eldrazi threats. Additionally, Aether Vial should have been activated to put a charge counter on it during upkeep - though looking at the choices, only Aether Vial activate and Wasteland activate are offered. The Aether Vial trigger happens automatically at beginning of upkeep, so that's separate. The key miss is declining to use Wasteland to destroy Eye of Ugin, which is a powerful cost-reduction land that will continue generating advantage for the Eldrazi player.

KimiK2 cast White Orchid Phantom before playing the Wasteland from hand. Playing the land first is free and provides an additional Wasteland activation to destroy a second nonbasic land from the opponent (who relies heavily on nonbasic lands like Eye of Ugin, Ancient Tomb, and Cavern of Souls). The creature could still be cast afterward with the same mana.

message: Select up to one nonbasic land
annotation_description: White Orchid Phantom's ETB is being used to destroy Eye of Ugin. While Eye of Ugin provides a cost reduction for colorless Eldrazi spells and a tutor ability, the opponent already has a Reality Smasher on board and Ancient Tomb still provides 2 colorless mana. Destroying Ancient Tomb would cut off the opponent's primary colorless mana source (2 mana per tap), making it much harder to cast future Eldrazi threats. Eye of Ugin only produces mana via its expensive 7-mana tutor activation and provides a 2-mana discount on Eldrazi spells, but with City of Traitors already in the graveyard and only Cavern of Souls + Ancient Tomb as mana sources, removing Ancient Tomb would be more crippling to the opponent's ability to cast spells at all. However, Eye of Ugin's cost reduction is powerful for chaining Eldrazi, so this is debatable.

message: Select a creature card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard
annotation_description: Pre-War Formalwear's ETB lets you return a creature with MV 3 or less from graveyard. The choice is between Phelia (2/2 flash, flickers permanents on attack) and Stoneforge Mystic (1/2, tutors equipment and cheats it in). KimiK2 already has Batterskull in hand, so Stoneforge's ETB tutor is less critical, but Stoneforge's activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}: put an Equipment from hand onto battlefield) would let them cheat Batterskull into play for just 1W instead of paying 5 mana. With all lands tapped this turn, neither creature can activate immediately, but Stoneforge would enable putting Batterskull into play next turn for just 1W (requiring only 2 mana), whereas without Stoneforge they need 5 mana for Batterskull. Phelia with Pre-War Formalwear becomes a 4/4 flash flier that can flicker things on attack, which is strong, but the opponent has Reality Smasher (5/5 trample haste) threatening lethal pressure. Getting Batterskull (4/4 vigilance lifelink germ) into play cheaply via Stoneforge seems more impactful for stabilizing at 14 life against a 5/5 trampler. However, Phelia could potentially flicker the opponent's Reality Smasher or Chalice of the Void, which has value too. The Aether Vial in hand is also dead due to Chalice on 0 countering it when cast — wait, Chalice is on 0 counters, and Aether Vial costs 1, so actually Aether Vial can be cast. This is debatable but Stoneforge enabling cheap Batterskull deployment seems stronger for the current board state.

Eldrazi Linebreaker costs {1}{C}{R}, requiring red mana. Cavern of Souls (chosen type: Eldrazi) can produce colored mana only for Eldrazi creature spells, so it can produce {R} for Linebreaker. However, casting Linebreaker consumes both Ancient Tombs (one tapped, one used for mana) and the Lotus Petal, leaving no mana to also cast Thought-Knot Seer this turn. Thought-Knot Seer (4/4) would strip a card from the opponent's hand, which is very valuable when the opponent has Aether Vial active and likely holding creatures like Phelia or other threats. Linebreaker's combat trigger gives +X/+0 where X is number of Eldrazi you control - with just Linebreaker and Reality Smasher, that's +2/+0 to one creature. Reality Smasher already has haste so it could attack regardless. The main question is whether Thought-Knot Seer's hand disruption (seeing and exiling a key card) would have been more impactful than Linebreaker's extra damage. With the opponent at 14 life and all lands tapped, the aggressive line is defensible, but TKS provides crucial information and disruption against an Aether Vial deck that will be vialing in creatures.

With opponent at 14 life and all their lands tapped, attacking with only Reality Smasher (8 damage) instead of all creatures leaves 3-5 points of damage on the table. Sending all attackers (Reality Smasher 8/5, Eldrazi Linebreaker 3/3, Glaring Fleshraker 2/2) forces opponent to make tough blocking decisions and maximizes pressure. White Orchid Phantom can only block one attacker, so most damage gets through.

Player chose to attack with only Reality Smasher instead of selecting 'All attack' which would have sent Eldrazi Linebreaker (which has haste) as well. Linebreaker as a 3/3 trampler could have dealt additional damage. Against an opponent at 14 life, the extra 3 damage (putting them to 5 instead of 8) is significant and could matter for closing out the game next turn.

KimiK2 Vorthos declined to activate any abilities at the beginning of their turn. They have two Wastelands available and the opponent has two Ancient Tombs and a Cavern of Souls as their only lands (all tapped). Destroying an Ancient Tomb now (before the opponent untaps next turn) would significantly limit the opponent's mana production and ability to cast more Eldrazi threats. The opponent is at 12 life and already losing life to Ancient Tomb, so denying mana is critical. Additionally, the Aether Vial is at 3 counters but they have no creature cards in hand (only Aether Vial and Batterskull), so that activation wouldn't help. But Wasteland on Ancient Tomb is a clear play - the opponent's explosive mana base is enabling powerful Eldrazi, and with Eye of Ugin and City of Traitors already in the graveyard, destroying an Ancient Tomb would leave them with very limited mana going forward.

chosen_display: Aether Vial — {T}: You may put a creature card with mana value ... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activated Aether Vial with no creature cards in hand, wasting the tap for the entire turn cycle. The activation resolves with nothing to put into play since the only card in hand is another Aether Vial (an artifact, not a creature).

Failed to block White Orchid Phantom (2/2) with Eldrazi Linebreaker (3/3), which would have killed the attacker while the Linebreaker survives. Instead took 2 unnecessary damage (12→10 life) and left the opponent's creature alive.

Casting Thought-Knot Seer pre-combat when lethal was already on board. With 3 Eldrazi, Linebreaker gives +3/+0 to Reality Smasher (8/5 trample) plus Linebreaker (3/3 trample) and Fleshraker (2/2) = 13 damage vs opponent at 10 life with all permanents tapped. White Orchid Phantom blocking only absorbs 2 damage with trample. Casting TKS first costs 2 life from Ancient Tomb (going to 8) and is unnecessary.

chosen_display: Aether Vial — {T}: You may put a creature card with mana value ... [Activate]
annotation_description: At 1 life facing lethal on board from Reality Smasher, Thought-Knot Seer, and other creatures, KimiK2 bounced their own Batterskull to hand, stripping their creature of +4/+4, vigilance, and critically lifelink. With 0 cards otherwise in hand and no way to quickly redeploy the 5-mana Batterskull, this leaves them unable to block effectively or gain life. The living weapon Germ token (if still alive) also dies as a 0/0.
